tour.name: Osaka Private Tour: Osaka Castle, Kuromon Market, Shinsekai & Dotonbori Street Food
tour.subtitle: A private day in Japan's kitchen with a licensed guide and car: Osaka Castle and its park, the stalls of Kuromon market, the retro district of Shinsekai and its kushikatsu, the Sumiyoshi Taisha shrine, and an evening of takoyaki and okonomiyaki under the neon lights of Dotonbori.

highlights: Osaka Castle, Hideyoshi's fortress, and its park
The retro district of Shinsekai and the Tsutenkaku tower
Kushikatsu, deep-fried skewers – but no double dipping!
Sumiyoshi Taisha and its arched red bridge
The neon lights and the Glico running man at night
tour.overview:
Osaka has been a city of merchants for centuries, the commercial heart of Japan when Edo was the political capital and Kyoto the imperial one. Its people are known for their humour, their straight talk and above all their love of food, summed up in the word kuidaore, 'to eat until you drop'. Toyotomi Hideyoshi, who unified Japan in the 16th century, built his great castle here, and the city's canals once carried rice from all over the country.

This private day shows the history and the appetite of Osaka with a licensed guide and a car. You visit the castle in the morning, taste your way through Kuromon market, see the 1910s-style district of Shinsekai and the oldest shrine of the city, and end in Dotonbori, where the canal is lined with giant signs, crab and puffer-fish models and street-food stalls.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 9 hours, ending in the evening
• Start and end: your hotel in Osaka
• Type: private tour with licensed guide, car and driver
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy; about 6 km on flat ground

WHAT YOU SEE
• Osaka Castle and Nishinomaru Garden.
• Kuromon market.
• Shinsekai and Tsutenkaku.
• Sumiyoshi Taisha.
• Dotonbori, Hozenji Yokocho and the Glico sign.

WHY THIS WORKS
We save Dotonbori for the evening, when the neon is lit and the food stalls are at their best, and use the car for the distances between the castle, the south and the shrine.

WHO IT SUITS
Food lovers, families and anyone who wants a fun, lively day after the temples of Kyoto.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you prefer temples and gardens, choose our Kyoto tours or Nara.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
Come hungry: the day includes many small tastings rather than one big lunch. Kuromon market is best in the late morning; many stalls close by late afternoon.

days.name: Osaka Castle, Kuromon market, Shinsekai, Sumiyoshi Taisha and an evening in Dotonbori
days.description:
What to expect: Osaka's castle and its legendary food culture, with a licensed guide, private car, castle ticket and many tastings.

Your guide and driver collect you at your hotel at about 10:00. You start at Osaka Castle, built from 1583 by Toyotomi Hideyoshi on a scale meant to impress all of Japan, with stones weighing over 100 tonnes in its walls. After his death it was besieged and burned by the Tokugawa in 1615; the main tower you see today, rebuilt in 1931, houses a museum of Hideyoshi's life, and the top floor gives a view over the city. You walk through the moats and gates and the park, with its plum and cherry orchards.

In Kuromon market, a covered street of some 150 stalls known as 'Osaka's kitchen', you taste grilled scallops, tuna, strawberries, wagyu skewers and tamagoyaki, the sweet rolled omelette. You continue to Shinsekai, a district built in 1912 on the model of Paris and New York, now a retro neighbourhood under the Tsutenkaku tower, where you eat kushikatsu, meat and vegetables on skewers, breaded and fried – with the strict rule never to dip twice in the shared sauce.

In the afternoon your driver takes you to Sumiyoshi Taisha, one of Japan's oldest shrines, founded according to tradition in 211, protector of sailors, with buildings in a style older than Buddhism in Japan and an arched red bridge over a pond. As night falls, you reach Dotonbori. Along the canal, giant signs – a mechanical crab, a puffer fish, the Glico running man lit since 1935 – glow above crowds and stalls. You taste takoyaki, octopus balls made in round iron pans, and okonomiyaki, and walk down Hozenji Yokocho, a stone-paved lane with a moss-covered statue of Fudo Myoo that people splash with water for luck. You are back at your hotel at about 19:00.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
10:00 – Pick-up at your hotel.
10:15 – Osaka Castle and its park.
12:00 – Kuromon market tastings.
13:30 – Shinsekai and kushikatsu.
15:00 – Sumiyoshi Taisha.
16:30 – Dotonbori and Hozenji Yokocho, street food and neon.
19:00 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• A Dotonbori canal cruise or a sake tasting can be added.
• Universal Studios Japan is a separate full day.
• Tell us about allergies and dietary needs; we adapt the tastings.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, licensed guide, Osaka Castle ticket, food tastings, bottled water, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: drinks, canal cruise.

Overnight: none.
Meals: tastings throughout the day.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: How much food is included?
faq.answer: Enough to replace lunch and an early dinner: a dozen or more tastings at the market, in Shinsekai and in Dotonbori.

faq.question: Can you adapt the food to our diet?
faq.answer: Yes. Tell us about vegetarian, halal, gluten-free or allergy needs and we plan the tastings accordingly.

faq.question: Are the entrance tickets included?
faq.answer: Yes, the Osaka Castle main tower. The shrines and markets are free.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Children love the castle, the giant signs and the street food. Child seats are provided free of charge on request.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Yes, largely. The castle has a lift, and the streets are flat. The car drops you close to each area.

faq.question: What is the rule about kushikatsu sauce?
faq.answer: Never dip twice in the shared sauce pot. Use a piece of cabbage to scoop more sauce if you need it.

faq.question: Can we add a day at Universal Studios?
faq.answer: We can book tickets, but the park needs a full day of its own.

faq.question: Can we combine Osaka with Nara?
faq.answer: Yes. Nara is 45 minutes away and makes an excellent separate day trip from Osaka.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tipping is not customary in Japan, and no one will expect it.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Comfortable shoes and casual clothes; come hungry.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: All year. Early April brings cherry blossom to the castle park; summer evenings in Dotonbori are hot but lively.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 72 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
